text: Chapter 3: Bearing Replacement Procedure. When vibration readings exceed 6.0 mm/s RMS at the motor drive end bearing, immediate inspection is required. Shut down the unit using the emergency stop procedure (section 2.1) before attempting any maintenance. Required tools: bearing puller set (P/N APX-TOOL-0047), torque wrench calibrated to 150 Nm, infrared thermometer.

Predictive indicators for bearing failure include: (1) gradual increase in vibration over 30-day window exceeding 15% trend, (2) temperature rise above baseline + 25°C sustained for more than 4 hours, (3) acoustic emission spikes above 70 dB during startup. If two or more indicators are present simultaneously, schedule maintenance within 48 hours.

Lubrication schedule for high-load applications: SKF LGHB 2 grease recommended. Relubrication interval: 2000 operating hours or 6 months whichever comes first. Quantity: 35g per bearing. Excess grease must be purged via the grease relief valve. Failure to follow lubrication schedule is the primary cause of premature bearing failure accounting for 47% of field failures.

Emergency shutdown sequence: 1) Activate E-STOP on local panel. 2) Verify motor current drops to zero within 3 seconds. 3) Lock out / Tag out per ISO 50001 procedure. 4) Allow 30 minutes cooling before access. Contact field service engineer if fault code E-0847 appears on HMI display after restart attempt.

Section 4.2 Service Level Agreement. Provider guarantees 99.95% uptime measured monthly excluding scheduled maintenance windows. Scheduled maintenance shall not exceed 4 hours per month and must be communicated with a minimum of 72 hours notice via the customer portal. Failure to meet SLA targets triggers automatic service credits as defined in Appendix B.

Section 7.1 Data Processing and GDPR Compliance. Provider acts as Data Processor under Article 28 GDPR. All personal data shall be processed exclusively within the European Economic Area unless explicitly authorized in writing. Provider maintains ISO 27001 certification and conducts annual penetration testing. Sub-processors are listed in Exhibit C and may be updated with 30 days notice.

Section 12.3 Limitation of Liability. Provider's aggregate liability for any claims arising under this agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid in the 12 months preceding the claim. This limitation does not apply to gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or breach of data protection obligations where liability is unlimited.

Section 15.1 Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate this agreement with 90 days written notice. Upon termination, Customer data will be returned in machine-readable format (CSV or JSON) within 30 days at no additional charge. Provider will maintain data for an additional 60 days before secure deletion per NIST 800-88 guidelines.

doc_title: EP4023891A1 - Method for Real-Time Fraud Detection Using Graph Neural Networks
text: Abstract: The present invention relates to a method and system for detecting fraudulent financial transactions in real-time using a graph neural network architecture. The method comprises: constructing a heterogeneous graph from transaction data wherein nodes represent entities including customers, merchants, devices and IP addresses; applying a message-passing neural network to propagate fraud signals through the graph; computing node-level fraud probability scores using attention mechanisms.

doc_title: EP4023891A1 - Method for Real-Time Fraud Detection Using Graph Neural Networks
text: Claim 1: A computer-implemented method for fraud detection comprising: receiving a stream of financial transaction events; for each transaction, constructing a local subgraph comprising the transaction entity and its k-hop neighborhood where k=2; applying a GraphSAGE encoder with 3 layers and 128-dimensional hidden representations; computing a fraud score in under 50 milliseconds latency.

doc_title: EP4023891A1 - Method for Real-Time Fraud Detection Using Graph Neural Networks
text: Technical Background: Traditional rule-based fraud detection systems suffer from high false positive rates (typically 15-30%) and inability to detect coordinated fraud rings. Graph-based approaches leverage relationship patterns that are invisible to per-transaction models. Experiments on a proprietary dataset of 47 million transactions show a 34% reduction in false positives while maintaining 94% recall at 0.5% false positive rate.

doc_title: EP4023891A1 - Method for Real-Time Fraud Detection Using Graph Neural Networks
text: Preferred Embodiment: The graph database is implemented using Elasticsearch with vector search capabilities, allowing approximate nearest-neighbor search on 512-dimensional entity embeddings. Entity embeddings are trained using a contrastive learning objective on co-occurrence patterns in transaction histories. The system processes 50,000 transactions per second on a 12-node cluster.
